Question 1

If z=3−4i, calculate z+z―.

a
6−8i
b
8i
c
7
d
6
e
12
Submit

decision.explanation: The conjugate of z=3-4i is 3+4i. Thus z+\overline{z}=(3-4i)+(3+4i)=6.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

When we add a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always twice the real part of the complex number.

For the given complex number $z=3-4\text{i},$ the real part is $Re(z)=3,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =2\text{Re}(z) \\  & =2(3) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of adding the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=3-4\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=3+4\text{i}.$

Adding, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =(3-4\text{i})+(3+4\text{i}) \\  & =(3+3)+\text{i}(-4+4) \\  & =6+\text{i}0 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

When we multiply a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always the sum of squares of the real part and the imaginary part.

For the given complex number $z=4+9\text{i},$ the real part is $\text{Re}(z)=4,$ and the imaginary part is $\text{Im}(z)=9,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(\text{Re}(z))^{2}+(\text{Im}(z))^{2} \\  & ={4}^{2}+{9}^{2} \\  & =16+81 \\  & =97.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of multiplying the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=4+9\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=4-9\text{i}.$

Multiplying, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(4+9\text{i})(4-9\text{i}) \\  & ={4}^{2}+(4)(-9)\text{i}+(4)(9)\text{i}-{\text{i}}^{2}(9)^{2} \\  & =16-36\text{i}+36\text{i}-(-1)(81) \\  & =16+81 \\  & =97.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: A complex number times its conjugate equals the sum of the squares of its real and imaginary parts: z\overline{z}=(-1)^2+(-7)^2=1+49=50.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

When we multiply a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always the sum of squares of the real part and the imaginary part.

For the given complex number $z=-1-7\text{i},$ the real part is $\text{Re}(z)=-1,$ and the imaginary part is $\text{Im}(z)=-7,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(\text{Re}(z))^{2}+(\text{Im}(z))^{2} \\  & =(-1)^{2}+(-7)^{2} \\  & =1+49 \\  & =50.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of multiplying the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=-1-7\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=-1+7\text{i}.$

Multiplying, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(-1-7\text{i})(-1+7\text{i}) \\  & =(-1)^{2}+(-1)(7)\text{i}+(-7)(-1)\text{i}-{\text{i}}^{2}(7)^{2} \\  & =1-7\text{i}+7\text{i}-(-1)(49) \\  & =1+49 \\  & =50.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

When we add a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always twice the real part of the complex number.

For the given complex number $z=-9-\text{i},$ the real part is $Re(z)=-9,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =2\text{Re}(z) \\  & =2(-9) \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of adding the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=-9-\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=-9+\text{i}.$

Adding, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =(-9-\text{i})+(-9+\text{i}) \\  & =(-9+(-9))+\text{i}(-1+1) \\  & =-18+\text{i}\cdot 0 \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$
